idiom_name: Sinatra route block per page (get '/orders' do ... end)
implementation_notes: Sinatra pairs an HTTP verb with a URL pattern and a block: get '/orders' do ... end is the page controller - it reads params, calls domain code and returns the response body, most often a rendered template (erb :orders). Routes are matched in definition order and each block runs in a per-request instance, so helpers declared with the helpers DSL stand in for the controller base class and before/after filters carry shared behaviour. Rails expresses the same page idea differently: a resource controller class whose actions are dispatched by the router, closer to Front Controller plus Application Controller; prefer the Sinatra/Rack form when pages, not resources, are the unit of the site.
code_sketch:
get '/orders' do
  require_login!                              # shared guard (helper)
  @orders = OrderService.list(current_user)   # domain logic
  erb :orders                                 # view selection
end

post '/orders' do
  OrderService.place(parse_order(params))     # domain logic
  redirect '/orders'                          # POST-redirect-GET
end
pitfalls: Routes are first-match-wins in definition order: a broad pattern declared before a specific page shadows it and the page appears to disappear.
Blocks are instance_eval'd per request, so plain methods defined in the file are not visible inside them - shared code must go through helpers or filters.
The block's return value is the response body: returning nil from a guard yields an empty 200, not an error, unless the guard halts or redirects explicitly.
